opamr: antibiotic prescribing data from OpenPrescribing, linked to the AMR package

Source: R/opamr-package.R
opamr-package.Rd

opamr has three layers:

  1. Crosswalk - ab_to_bnf(), bnf_to_ab(), atc_to_bnf(), bnf_to_atc() and op_antibiotics() move between antimicrobial names / AMR package codes / ATC codes and BNF chemical codes, using the bundled antibiotic_crosswalk table. The AMR package is optional: it is only used to resolve free-text names, synonyms and brand names that the bundled table does not recognise.

  2. Data access - op_spending(), op_spending_ab(), op_org_details(), op_rate(), op_antibiotic_use(), op_bnf_search() and op_org_search() wrap the OpenPrescribing API.

  3. Figures - theme_op(), scale_colour_op(), op_plot_trend(), op_plot_seasonal(), op_plot_distribution(), op_plot_heatmap() and op_save().

Data source and licence

Prescribing data are published monthly by the NHS Business Services Authority under the Open Government Licence v3.0 and served by the Bennett Institute for Applied Data Science (University of Oxford) through OpenPrescribing. Cite both when publishing. The data cover prescriptions issued in English primary care and dispensed in the community; they contain items, quantities and costs, not indications, doses or patients.

Options

  • opamr.base_url - API root (default https://openprescribing.net/api/1.0).

  • opamr.rate - maximum requests per second (default 2; Inf disables throttling).

  • opamr.cache - cache responses for the R session (default TRUE).

  • opamr.cache_dir - optional directory for a persistent on-disk response cache.

  • opamr.timeout - request timeout in seconds (default 120).

  • opamr.max_tries - attempts for transient failures (HTTP 429/5xx; default 3).

  • opamr.retry_wait - seconds to wait between attempts (default exponential: 2, 4, ...).
